utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-R77.1-T, In the Matter of Ljubisa Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today is Thursday, the 11th of September, 2008. Good afternoon, Mr. Petkovic; good afternoon to your Defence counsel, and good afternoon to everyone assisting us in this courtroom. The registrar, the court deputy, and everyone else. The Trial Chamber is now going to deliver its Judgement in the case of contempt against Mr. Ljubisa Petkovic. Mr. Petkovic, would you please stand whilst I read out the Judgement in your case. Today, Thursday, 11th of September 2008, the Trial Chamber, consisting of Jean-Claude Antonetti, president, Frederik Harhoff and Flavia Lattanzi is delivering its judgement on the allegations against Ljubisa Petkovic, the accused, pursuant to Article 77(A)(iii) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. This is only a summary which does not form part of the Judgement delivered by the Trial Chamber. The only authorative account of the Trial Chamber's findings is in the written Judgement, copies of which will be available after the hearing. The accused and the Defence will be given a confidential version of the Judgement while a public redacted version will be available to the public. 77(A)(iii) reads, and I quote: "(A) The Tribunal, in the exercise of its inherent power, may hold in contempt those who knowingly and willfully interfere with its administration of justice, including any person ... who without just excuse fails to comply with an order to attend before or produce documents before a Chamber." The accused is charged with having knowingly and willfully interfered with the administration of justice by refusing to comply with the subpoena issued on 7th of April, 2008, proprio motu and confidentially by the Trial Chamber in the case against Vojislav Seselj. This subpoena ordered Ljubisa Petkovic to appear before the Trial Chamber as of 13th of May, 2008, as a "chamber witness." The accused having failed to do so, the Trial Chamber decided to initiate the proceedings itself. The trial was held on the 3rd of September, and the Defence put forward two witnesses, the accused and his wife. The Defence of Ljubisa Petkovic acknowledged that the actus reus of the offence of contempt as described in 77(A)(iii) of the Rules was constituted by the mere fact that the accused failed to appear at the time and location indicated by the Trial Chamber. The Trial Chamber equally considers that the actus reus of the offence of contempt is constituted by the absence of the accused at the hearing of 13 May 2008. The Trial Chamber thereafter considered whether the circumstances surrounding the notification of the subpoena and the deterioration of the state of health of the accused could amount to "just excuse" pursuant to Rule 77(A)(iii) of the Rules, as submitted by the Defence in support of its contention that the accused should be acquitted. The Trial Chamber considers that the accused has not established the existence of just excuses pursuant to 77(A)(iii) of the Rules. First, considering all the elements in its possession, or his possession, the accused could not reasonably doubt that he was the addressee of the subpoena. Secondly, though psychologically fragile, the accused was not in a state of health which prevented him from informing the Trial Chamber that he could not comply with the subpoena. Moreover, the Trial Chamber considers that the mens rea of the offence is constituted by the fact that the accused, instead of complying with the obligations imposed on him by the subpoena, voluntarily failed to execute it by choosing to escape, without just excuses. As a consequence, he knowingly and willfully interfered with the administration of justice. Therefore, the Trial Chamber is satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that the accused is guilty of the offence of contempt, pursuant to 77(A)(iii) of the Rules. In its determination of the sentence, the Trial Chamber took into account the gravity of the offence, the general sentencing practice of the courts of the former Yugoslavia, and the jurisprudence of the Tribunal, as well as the aggravating circumstance constituted by the failure of the accused to comply, for the second time, with an order of the Trial Chamber. Due consideration was also given to the following mitigating circumstances: The absence of any prior criminal history; the facts that the accused voiced excuses for his conduct and the family; and personal circumstances of the accused. In that regard, when determining the sentence, the Trial Chamber took into account the financial situation of the accused. Before reading the disposition, the Trial Chamber wishes to underline the gravity of the offence for which the accused is found guilty. In that regard, the Trial Chamber wishes to recall that witnesses are not the property of the parties and that when the Trial Chamber decides, by way of a subpoena, that their testimony is necessary to establish the truth, they have to comply with it. When ordered to appear as a Trial Chamber witness, pursuant to Rule 98 of the Rules, the accused could not refuse to comply with the subpoena by stating that he was, and I quote, "'a Defence witness." For the reasons summarized above, having taken into consideration the totality of the arguments and evidence presented by the Defence, the Trial Chamber decides that, pursuant to Rule 77 of the Rules: (i) the accused Ljubisa Petkovic is guilty of contempt of the Tribunal, punishable pursuant to 77(A)(iii) of the Rules; (ii) the accused Ljubisa Petkovic is sentenced to four months of imprisonment, credit being given to the three months and 14 days spent in detention at the United Nations Detention Unit; (iii) the registry shall take all necessary measures for the accused to serve his sense. The summary of the Judgement in this case has been read out, and we are now going to adjourn. Thank you very much.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.27 p.m.
